info.title: Medad REST API Documentation
info.summary: Combined RESTful API documentation for all DocTypes and API Methods
info.description: This specification provides comprehensive API documentation for all DocTypes and whitelisted API methods in the Medad system. Use the standard Frappe REST API patterns to interact with documents.

skip_authorization.description: If checked, users will not see the Confirm Access dialog.

scopes.description:
A list of resources which the Client App will have access to after the user allows it.
e.g. project

redirect_uris.description:
URIs for receiving authorization code once the user allows access, as well as failure responses. Typically a REST endpoint exposed by the Client App.
e.g. http://hostname/api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2_logins.login_via_facebook

client_uri.description: URL of a web page providing information about the client.

software_id.description:
Unique ID assigned by the client developer used to identify the client software to be dynamically registered.
Should remain same across multiple versions or updates of the software.

tos_uri.description: URL that points to a human-readable terms of service document for the client. Should be shown to end-user before authorizing.

contacts.description: New lines separated list of strings representing ways to contact people responsible for this client, typically email addresses.

logo_uri.description: URL that references a logo for the client.

software_version.description:
A version identifier string for the client software.
The value of the should change on any update of the client software with the same Software ID.

policy_uri.description: URL that points to a human-readable policy document for the client. Should be shown to end-user before authorizing.

token_endpoint_auth_method.description: Value of "None" implies a public client. In such a case Client Secret is not given to the client and token exchange makes use of PKCE.

formula.description:
How to write a formula:
  • A simple formula that should return either a numeric or a Boolean (true or false) value.
  • Use the syntax: field_name whenever you want to refer to a field that exists in the form, example: gpa or gender.
  • The fields available are the ones defined in the Applicant DocType or those included in the Model that is using this Formula.
  • To check a field's value, you can use comparison operators, such as: ==, !=, >, <, >= or <=.
  • To check multiple conditions, you can use logical operators, such as: and or or.
  • You can use arithmetic operators to calculate values, such as: +, -, *, / or %.
  • You can also use parentheses to group conditions, example: condition1 and (condition2 or condition3).
  • You must surround words with double quotation marks, example: gender == "Male" or some_field != "Some unwanted value".

Formula Variables Reference:
  • valid: Returns 0 or 1
  • score: Returns float
  • excluded: Returns 0 or 1, but score must exist also
  • message: Returns string - A descriptive message that provides context about the calculation (optional, can be empty)

python_script.description:
Available variables:
  • student_id: The ID of eligible student to check whether he/she is excluded or not from the Stipend in question.
  • academic_term: The Academic Term to use to make complex query in the Stipend in question.
  • term_used_for_gpa: The Academic Term Used for GPA to use to make complex query in the Stipend in question.

To use the variable call it directly: variable (e.g. student_id).


Exemple:
student_term_gpa = frappe.db.get_value('Student GPA', {'student': student_id, 'academic_term': academic_term}, ['term_gpa']))
excluded = student_term_gpa<2

formula.description:
How to write a formula:
  • A simple formula that should return either a numeric or a Boolean (true or false) value.
  • Use the syntax: data.field_name whenever you want to refer to a field that exists in the form, example: data.gpa or data.gender.
  • The fields available are the ones defined in the Applicant DocType or those included in the Model that is using this Formula.
  • To check a field's value, you can use comparison operators, such as: ==, !=, >, <, >= or <=.
  • To check multiple conditions, you can use logical operators, such as: and or or.
  • You can use arithmetic operators to calculate values, such as: +, -, *, / or %.
  • You can also use parentheses to group conditions, example: condition1 and (condition2 or condition3).
  • You must surround words with double quotation marks, example: gender == "Male" or some_field != "Some unwanted value".
